doc.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Dave Brubeck, Greek rhythms and preparing for Ellis's music
summary: Rowe cites Brubeck and Greek music; Humphrey says playing along with Brubeck records prepared him for Don Ellis's music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: You know I recall Dave Brubeck talking about hearing Greek music and that’s what inspired him to do [scats].
Yes of course. That’s a primary Greek rhythm right there.
Did those albums have an effect on you?

Yeah they did. I mean I guess I must have subjectively understood what it was. I didn’t objectively be able to explain except I just heard it and I played along with those records and tried to learn as much about it as possible. And I think that was probably the main reason why I was able to approach Don Ellis’ music was because of that. Because not only was I enjoying the music of Dave Brubeck but I was investigating it as well. I wanted to know what it was that was going on there. And I don’t know where that comes from. It’s just one person’s desire to know something.
Yeah. Well it’s pretty cool he’s still out there doing it.
That’s right. And his sons and whatnot.
